# YM05: 天然图画 Tianran Tuhua, "A Painting by Nature"

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM05` · Page: `/scenes/#YM05` · Row: `research/buildings/YM05-tianran-tuhua/`

## What it was

天然图画 Tianran Tuhua, on the east bank of the Back Lake north of 镂月开云: the tower 天然图画楼, with 朗吟阁 Langyin Ge to the north, 竹薖楼 Zhuke Lou further north, 五福堂 Wufu Tang of five bays to the east, a five-bay hall 竹深荷净 Zhushen Hejing behind it to the north, 静知春事佳 Jingzhi Chunshi Jia to the south-east, and across the stream 苏堤春晓 Sudi Chunxiao (S05 j80:31b). Most plaques are by Yongzheng; that of 五福堂 by Kangxi, so the core predates 1723 (S05 j80:32a). The garden was burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188), but 文昌阁 Wenchang Ge (YM05-08, tie 'likely') stood among the 17 buildings 刘敦桢 listed as left after the fire in 1933 (E0451, S337).

From the inventory row: **changed** South pool and islet filled, probably c. 1831; pool found by excavation (S41). Not in the 1860 state.; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S41, S01).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Preface of 1744: "庭前修篁萬竿與雙桐相暎風枝露梢緑滿襟䄂西為髙樓折而南翼以重榭" (S05 j80:32b). Ten thousand bamboos and two paulownias in the court; a tall tower on the west, turning south into two-storey pavilions, with distant views beyond what a painter could do. The poem warns against carved walls and lofty halls even while praising them.

### How later sources differ

五福堂 was renamed 五福五代堂 in 甲辰 1784, when Qianlong, then past seventy, saw his great-great-grandson: 'in 甲辰 I saw my 元孙 and added two characters, 五福五代堂' (E1225, S360, 1790 poem note). The plaque 五福堂 was Kangxi's, given to Yongzheng and hung first in his princely residence, now 雍和宫 (E1226). S01 writes 五福五代堂 (YM05-04): so the plan is post-1784. 竹深荷净 (YM05-05) carries a label read "?静斋" on an 11-cell row, another post-S05 change.

## Interior and setting

### Interior

Nothing written yet.

### The garden around it

Bamboo grove and twin paulownias in the court, the Back Lake to the west, a stream to the east crossed to 苏堤春晓, named after the Su causeway of West Lake (S05 j80:31b-32b). 竹薖楼 had an eave plaque 桃花春一溪 by Yongzheng, i.e. peach trees along a stream (S05 j80:32a).
